/products / 01 · AI tools · Fintech

Lender-ready analytics decks, assembled from the source data

A credit analytics company reports to the country's largest banks. Each deck took about 80 hours by hand. Now the first draft builds from the data in minutes, and revisions apply across the whole deck.

Product from zero: knowledge base, templates, revision engine

Sheet 03 · How it was solved

problem · decision · build · change

The problem

Every report began as an Excel workbook. Someone rebuilt it by hand into 40–60 slides with up to ~290 charts, then spent a week on revisions: the same fix on twenty slides, five to twelve versions per deck.

The product decision

Don't automate slides, automate the source. Templates were derived from 30+ finished decks, so every chart and table is generated from the workbook, and every revision goes to the source and flows to every slide.

What we built

Excel in, branded deck out: charts, tables, takeaways, group legends · revisions by plain-language command or by notes on the PDF · diagrams drawn in Excel moved to slides one to one · PDF for the client and editable PPTX.

What changed

About 10× faster end to end. The analyst checks the story the numbers tell instead of retyping them, and slides can no longer drift out of sync with the workbook.

short deadline, full responsibility

  1. Before

    ~10 years of decks built by hand

  2. Step 1

    30+ decks and workbooks analysed

  3. Step 2

    Templates and revision engine

  4. Today

    Draft in minutes, ≈10× faster

Sheet 03 · How it was solved

problem · decision · build · change

The problem — two sides

The owner had GPU servers standing idle: a cost with no revenue. Companies wanted LLMs but couldn't send sensitive data to foreign clouds, and didn't want a subscription for occasional tasks.

The product decision

Don't rent out servers, sell tokens. A catalogue of open models, each priced per token: clients pick the right model per task, the owner fills the GPUs with many small loads.

What we built

Model catalogue and one API · per-token billing, no subscription · isolation that keeps data inside the jurisdiction · load balancing across the owner's servers.

What changed

Idle hardware became a revenue line at 80% load. Clients got LLMs for sensitive data without moving it abroad, and pay only for what they use.

Sheet 03 · How it was solved

problem · decision · build · change

The problem

Airlines search for pilots through agents, spreadsheets and chats. Pilots fill in the same forms again and again, and good matches are found late.

The product decision

Let a vacancy go live from a few inputs that matter — total and night hours, base, rank, type ratings — and let AI do the first screening, so people only talk to likely matches.

What we built

Pilot profiles · vacancy builder · AI matching and shortlist · the flow from first contact to interview.

What changed

Sheet 03 · How it was solved

problem · decision · build · change

The problem

The format was returning to prime time on a fixed date, produced without the original software. Live TV allows no second take.

The product decision

Treat it as broadcast equipment, not an app: one system for the operator console, game logic and on-air graphics, with fail-safes tested before every recording.

What we built

Operator console · game logic engine · on-air graphics · redundancy and rehearsal mode.

What changed

On air since April 2023, four seasons and 50+ episodes without a single failure. Nominated for the national TV award in 2023 and 2026.

problem · decision · build · change

The product decision

A purpose-built scoring tool for the field instead of spreadsheets: each judge enters scores on a device, totals compute instantly, screens and broadcast read the same source.

What we built

Judge app · scoring engine · live leaderboard output for screens and the host.

Sheet 03 · How it was solved

problem · decision · build · change

The problem

A new kind of attraction with no reference to copy, a large public budget and a state expert review to pass.

The product decision

Mixed reality instead of pure VR: the physical set, props and effects carry the immersion, so content and hardware are designed as one product.

What we built

Realistic content that continues the set · wireless VR for free movement · rain, wind, heat and cold, haptic vests and guns, a tilting platform, players' own hands in the game.

What changed

Passed the expert review; tickets sell out two weeks ahead, every week since opening.

Sheet 03 · How it was solved

problem · decision · build · change

The problem

A touring exhibition needs an interactive zone that survives packing, shipping and re-installation, and runs every day without an engineer on site.

The product decision

Design the zone as a product, not a one-off: the same content, hardware kit and install procedure for every venue.

What we built

Interactive floor projection of moving ants · tracking and projection setup · a repeatable install by one team.

What changed

The attraction ran 7.5 years on the Las Vegas Strip (June 2016 – January 2024) and was named "Best Place to Meet Your Heroes" by Vegas Seven.
